alberdilabr scaffolds reproducible publication websites. It creates the
project, keeps chapter files and their ordering in step, validates the result,
and wires up deployment to GitHub Pages.

It does not render anything itself. Rendering belongs to
[bookdown](https://bookdown.org), dependency pinning to
[renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/), and deployment to GitHub Actions. The
project you get is an ordinary bookdown project that builds with
`bookdown::render_book()` whether or not this package is installed.

## Create a project

```r
library(alberdilabr)

create_publication(
  path   = "my-analysis",
  title  = "My Analysis",
  author = "Jane Doe"
)
```

That produces:

```text
my-analysis/
├── my-analysis.Rproj
├── index.Rmd              landing page and shared YAML front matter
├── _bookdown.yml          chapter order and output directory
├── _output.yml            bookdown::bs4_book configuration
├── README.md
├── references.bib
├── .gitignore
├── chapters/
│   ├── 01-introduction.Rmd
│   ├── 02-methods.Rmd
│   ├── 03-results.Rmd
│   └── 04-discussion.Rmd
├── R/setup.R              options and libraries shared by every chapter
├── data/
├── figures/
├── assets/style.css
└── .github/workflows/publish.yml
```

`create_publication()` also initialises Git and, unless you pass
`renv = FALSE`, an renv lockfile.

## Write

Add a chapter and it is created, numbered and registered in `_bookdown.yml` in
one step:

```r
add_chapter("Sensitivity analysis")
#> v Added chapter "sensitivity-analysis" at 'chapters/05-sensitivity-analysis.Rmd'.
```

Insert one in the middle and the chapters after it are renumbered to match:

```r
add_chapter("Study design", after = "introduction", template = "methods")
```

Reorder and remove chapters the same way. Every one of these keeps the files on
disk and the `rmd_files` list in `_bookdown.yml` consistent:

```r
move_chapter("discussion", after = "results")
remove_chapter("sensitivity-analysis")
```

Chapters are addressed by their slug (`"discussion"`), their filename
(`"04-discussion.Rmd"`) or their path. See `chapter_templates()` for the
starter templates.

## Preview

```r
preview_publication()
```

This starts `bookdown::serve_book()`, which re-renders the chapter you are
editing and reloads the browser. It is much faster than a full build, at the
cost of occasionally stale cross-references between chapters.

For a full production build:

```r
render_publication()
```

The site is written to `_site/`.

## Validate

```r
check_publication()
```

```text
-- Structure --
v index.Rmd exists
v 5 chapters registered in _bookdown.yml
v all registered files exist
v no unregistered chapter files

-- Documents --
v every chapter has exactly one top-level heading
v chapter identifiers are unique
! chapters/03-results.Rmd contains an unlabelled figure

-- Publishing --
v workflow uploads _site/, matching output_dir
```

Checks cover project structure, document structure (one top-level heading per
chapter, unique heading identifiers and chunk labels, figures that can be
cross-referenced), reproducibility, and agreement between the directory
bookdown writes and the one the workflow uploads. No network access is
performed.

Add a full build as an integration test with:

```r
check_publication(render = TRUE)
```

## Publish

The generated workflow renders the book on every push to `main` and uploads
`_site/` as a GitHub Pages artifact. Rendered HTML is never committed.

One manual step is required the first time: in the repository, go to
**Settings → Pages → Build and deployment** and set **Source** to
**GitHub Actions**.

If you created the project with `renv = FALSE` and later want pinned
dependencies:

```r
renv::init()
use_github_publication(overwrite = TRUE)
```

`use_github_publication()` detects the lockfile and writes the workflow that
restores from it.
